# NOTES: *Feathers Left Around* by Carolyn Wells (1923, Lippincott). Fleming Stone detective novel. Single book, no multi-book split.

## Front matter
- Gutenberg #75642. Dedication: "To my dear friend Adala Wilson." Other Stone titles listed: The Mystery Girl, Mystery of the Sycamore, Raspberry Jam, Diamond Pin, Vicky Van, Mark of Cain, Curved Blades, White Alley, Anybody But Anne, Maxwell Mystery, Chain of Evidence, The Clue, Gold Bag, Ptomaine Street (parody).
- Contents: Ch I Little Anna; II A Celebrated Guest; III The Tragedy; IV The Meredith Story; V Roly Takes the Lead; VI What Tessie Saw; VII The Sister Arrives; VIII Little Anna's Wiles; IX Pauline's Grief; X Curran's Watch; XI Pauline's Flight; XII With Mary Malden; XIII How Loft Took It; XIV Fibsy Meets a Countess; XV The Needle Again; XVI Curran's Cruelty; XVII On to Mapledale; XVIII The Truth at Last.

## Characters
- **Valentine "Val" Loft**: host of "Valhalla" (Anna's name for his Westchester County estate). 32, lawyer/real-estate/architect/financier. Motto "Do nothing and all things will be done." Strongly anti-divorce. Engaged to Pauline Fuller.
- **Pauline Fuller**: tall, dark, beautiful, black eyebrows, fiancée. Former married name Mrs. Hugh Dwyer; married at 17 (about 8 months courtship) to Hugh Dwyer, eloped, cruel husband; divorced in Reno ~6 years earlier (courts restored maiden name). Nickname "Rosalie"/"Rosy" (Dwyer's name for her, for pink cheeks); Loft's "Pearline"/"Pauly." Her aunt in NY is ill/nervous.
- **Hugh Curran** (real name Hugh Dwyer): detective-story author, ex-movie character actor (Indiana-born, lived CA). Divorced. Round red face, sandy hair, gray roving eyes, thickset. Untidy. Fiancée Miss Fitzgerald of Chicago. Found dead in locked room, sitting in arm chair, fully dressed, Sat. morning. Died ~4–5 AM.
- **Anna Knox** ("Little Anna"): blonde, flirt, wife of Ned Knox, chaperone. Separate rooms with bath between her and Ned; her room opens on balcony. Sought Curran's attention.
- **Ned Knox**: small, athletic, egotistical, writes detective short stories. Jealous of Anna. Overheard Bob & Curran arguing about "a needle."
- **Angel Bob Baldwin**: giant Viking-type, blue eyes, rare-book dealer under fictitious firm "Baldwin and Co." Amateur photographer with poison in photographic outfit in Loft's den. Actual culprit (see below).
- **Countess Galaski**: Russian, rouged, sharp-tongued, kind heart, wears white satin.
- **Stella Lawrence**: ash-blonde, trailing draperies, psychic/dreamer. Dreamed of "Rosalie" and "Mr. S." books.
- **Roly Mears**: young, incorrigible, amateur sleuth, takes lead.
- **Jim Martin**: friend who rebuked Loft about divorce.
- **Mr. & Mrs. Jack Meredith**: colorless middle-aged couple. Mr. Meredith heard footsteps, saw a shawled woman enter Curran's room ~half past one/two, heard door open again ~2:30.
- **Binns**: butler. **Mrs. Jennings**: housekeeper. **Bates**: chauffeur. **Gideon**: night watchman.
- **Tessie**: chambermaid, out late night before; claims she saw Anna & Curran on balcony (Anna in rosebud negligée). Violet: parlor maid, Tessie's roommate.
- **Doctor Gilvray**: County Medical Examiner. Determined cause: hydrocyanic (Prussic) acid, mouth odor, none in stomach.
- **Detective Kinney**: local detective; infatuated with Anna; suspects Pauline; finds watch.
- **Jackson**: detective who reported on Curran (born Indiana, Hugh Dwyer legally, Grampian Annex hotel NY, A-1 rating).
- **Hetty (Hester) Dwyer**: Curran's spinster sister, tall, angular, quill-hat, claims inheritance, suspects Loft. Dislikes Countess.
- **Mary Malden**: Pauline's old school friend's spinster, farm in Mapledale, Berkshires village.
- **Fleming Stone**: great American detective. **Terence "Fibsy" McGuire**: his Irish red-haired, freckled assistant, ~teen.
- **Mrs. Meredith**: busybody.

## Key events in order
1. Ch I: Party at Valhalla. Discussion of murder methods (strangling - Bob, shooting - Ned, stabbing with paper-cutter, poison - Pauline). Loft invites Curran. Anna speaks of "feathers left around" (not yet). Ned says Curran salts food first.
2. Ch II: Curran arrives. Says circumstantial evidence = "feathers left around" (chicken anecdote, "old darkey"). Countess, Stella, Roly present. Curran walks with Anna & Bob; talks rare books. Anna reveals to Curran she's married; Curran says he's divorced (Reno). Bob warns not to mention divorce to Loft.
3. Ch III: Dinner. Curran asks butler for toothpick (Binns gives Japanese wooden one). Party in library: Curran "clairvoyance": "Black Pansy" (Ned's mine), "Rosalie" (no reaction), "Mr. S." Pauline reacts. Next morning Curran doesn't appear. Loft, Binns, Bob, Ned go up; door locked; Binns climbs ladder to window (fastened). Break in door; Curran dead in chair, dressed.
4. Ch IV: Gilvray diagnoses Prussic acid; Kinney called. Loft tells Pauline (she faints; reluctant to be questioned). Household questioned. Meredith testifies about shawled woman. Anna denies being out.
5. Ch V: Roly leads "detective squad" (Loft, Ned, Angel, Roly). Search room. Items: salted almond basket (Bob brought up at ~12:15, left ~12:40–12:45 after discussing Caxton "Book of the Noble History of King Arthur" 1485). Bob gave Curran a Country Club toothpick paper. Torn papers. Watch missing (Stella/Bob/Countess saw it, pictures of woman inside).
6. Ch VI: Ned tells Roly that Bob & Curran quarrelled about a "needle" (Ned suggests hypodermic). Jackson's report: Curran was film actor ~6 yrs, writer 2 yrs; real name Hugh Dwyer. Violet/Tessie reveal Anna on balcony with Curran after one o'clock. Bob threatens Violet.
7. Ch VII: Loft's theory Ned did it. Hetty Dwyer arrives, sister of Curran; says he was about to marry Miss Fitzgerald of Chicago; claims Rosalie was his ex-wife (no name known). Hetty suspects society guests. Pauline reveals watch picture not Anna's; it's a young girl with curly hair (Pauline's face).
8. Ch VIII: Roly proposes unseen intruder. Kinney interviews Anna, who charms him, claims a knock on Curran's door by a woman. Kinney favors Anna's story. Stella's dream ("Rosalie," "Mr. S."). Hetty suggests book-collector motive. Bob defends collectors. Loft/Angel suspicious of Tessie; Tessie & Violet alibi.
9. Ch IX: Kinney suspects Ned posing as woman. Countess tells Kinney to search rooms. Kinney hears Pauline sobbing "I must forget...I have forgotten." Tessie claims was making bed. Kinney searches Pauline's locked desk (picks lock), finds Curran's watch. Bob sees Pauline's picture inside. Bob cries "Pauline!"
10. Ch X: Loft furious at Kinney; insists on seeing Pauline himself. Loft: picture is school-girl photo; Kinney keeps watch. Countess says Rosalie nickname; hints Anna's malice. Hetty wants Loft as suspect. Countess believes Pauline in hall. Kinney goes to Loft at 5 PM: Pauline has gone.
11. Ch XI: Pauline left on 4:45 train to NY (Bates drove her, Tessie along; Tessie given packing instructions; note "Good-by" to Loft). Loft believes she left train, went other direction. Loft tells Angel he will find her. Kinney telephones police. Guests speculate (Stella: Pauline corresponded with Curran; Anna: sent photo). Bob warns Kinney to find Curran's ex-wife in Reno.
12. Ch XII: Loft calls NY home (aunt ill). Stella tells Loft Pauline came out of Curran's room at 2:30; Loft dismisses Stella from house (4 PM train). Countess tells Loft she saw Pauline (not fully certain) carrying glittering item. Pauline at Mary Malden's farm in Berkshires (Mapledale). Loft has laid "plans." Reno report: Hugh Dwyer married Pauline Fuller ~8 months, divorced ~6 years earlier.
13. Ch XIII: Loft reels from news. Recalls Curran's "Are you untidy about bureau drawers?"; hypothesizes Pauline killed Curran. Loft tells Anna he's always her friend. Hetty hostile. Loft proposes to confess to Curran's murder (sham) to shield Pauline; Angel, Ned, Roly refuse. Roly proposes Fleming Stone.
14. Ch XIV: Stone & Fibsy arrive at Valhalla. Loft: wants proof of innocence or concealment. Stone agrees, won't compound felony. Countess tells Stone she saw Pauline with watch. Stone's alibi analysis. Miss Dwyer hostile. Stone: killers who talk methods; "feathers" metaphor. Fibsy charms Countess.
15. Ch XV: Stone & Roly visit Gilvray; Gilvray says poison administered orally, no stomach traces. Stone wants to examine body. Loft's theory Pauline hidden in New England farmhouse. Stone & Fibsy search room, waste-basket (inventory: torn papers, string, pencil shavings, cigarette box, digestive tablets box, wooden toothpick, quill toothpick, torn toothpick paper, burnt matches, envelopes). Fibsy's radio plan. Fibsy gets Tessie to reveal NY Central Harlem Division timetable in bag. Loft gives Fibsy $500 and message "There's a Valentine waiting for Pauline" / "The Portuguese are the people!" Fibsy to Springfield.
16. Ch XVI: Pauline with Mary. Her story: married Dwyer at 17 (eloped), divorced after 8 months; she visited Curran (Dwyer) at 2 AM at his request; he begged her to remarry him; she grabbed watch and letters and fled. Curran alive then. Radio: "The Portuguese are the people!" "Pearline, come back, I love you," "There's a Valentine a waiting for Pauline" (baritone song). Pauline phones Loft.
17. Ch XVII: Loft drives to Mapledale with Fibsy (~midnight). Fibsy reveals radio ruse. Loft & Pauline reunite. Pauline says she did not kill Curran. They marry at Mary's (Rev. Dr. Messiter). Return by noon. Stone sends Fibsy to NY to buy a page (Gammer Gurton's Needle title page); Bob buys it (~$200 limit). Stone: "The case is about finished."
18. Ch XVIII: Dinner wedding feast. Kinney arrives 9 PM. Stone's solution: Bob Baldwin stole pages from Curran's rare book "Gammer Gurton's Needle" (1575, Thomas Colwell), photographed/substituted pages, sold a completed copy for $20,000. Curran threatened exposure; Bob used a poisoned quill toothpick (poison from photo outfit) via puncture in jaw inside mouth; substituted clean toothpick in waste-basket; "Mr. S." = author's title page "by Mr. S." Bob confesses, swallows poison, dies. Loft & Pauline leave on honeymoon; Kinney takes charge of Bob's body.

END. (Transcriber's notes: typos corrected.)
